name: King Island
note: Island destination: Bass Strait island, reached by air from Melbourne, Launceston, Burnie or Hobart; the base for everything on King Island.

name: Currie
note: Town: the largest town on King Island, with the visitor centre, the King Island Museum and the Currie Lighthouse.

name: Naracoopa
note: Town: small east-coast settlement on Sea Elephant Bay, with a restaurant and beach-front cottages.

name: Grassy
note: Town: settlement on King Island's south-west, home of the Wild Harvest restaurant and a former scheelite mine.

name: Cape Wickham Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse: Australia's tallest at 48 m, on the north-west cape, built 1861 after the Cataraqui wreck; climbable on tours, with a small church and gravestones beside it.

name: Calcified Forest
note: Walk: 30-minute, 1.3 km Great Short Walk through calcified limestone features of a 7000-year-old forest.

name: Seal Rocks
note: Coastal lookout: rugged coastline with the island's highest cliffs, about 60 m above the sea, reached by a short walk; the Copperhead Track runs north from it.

name: Martha Lavinia Beach
note: Beach: north-east coast surf beach, rated among the world's best surf breaks by Surfing Life, with walking and beachcombing.

name: Sea Elephant Bay
note: Beach: bay on King Island's east coast at Naracoopa, named in the Wikivoyage listings for its accommodation.

name: Currie Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse: harbour lighthouse at Currie (built 1879), beside the colourful boathouse restaurant.

name: King Island Historical Museum
note: Museum: in the old lighthouse keeper's cottage at Currie, with shipwreck and sealing history, the scheelite mine and the original Cape Wickham lens.

name: King Island Maritime Trail
note: Trail: self-guided route (brochure from Currie visitor centre) past eight shipwreck sites and the island's lighthouses and safe havens; a route, not a single place.

name: Cataraqui
note: Shipwreck site: the 1845 wreck of the barque Cataraqui, Australia's worst peacetime maritime disaster, on the Maritime Trail.

name: King Island Dairy
note: Dairy shop: cheese shop and tasting at the King Island Dairy, less than 10 minutes north of Currie; a shop, not a sight.

name: Cape Wickham Golf Links
note: Golf course: links course ranked Australia's top course by Australian Golf Digest 2024/25, open to visitors.

name: Ocean Dunes Golf Course
note: Golf course: links course on King Island, ranked in the top 15 in Australia by Australian Golf Digest.

name: The Boathouse Restaurant With No Food
note: Restaurant: colourful boathouse in Currie where diners bring their own food; a quirky venue, a restaurant first.

name: Wild Harvest
note: Restaurant: paddock-to-plate fine dining in Grassy on King Island; a restaurant, not an attraction.

name: King Island Distillery
note: Distillery: native gin and ruby vodka, with tours and tastings by arrangement.

name: King Island Brewhouse
note: Brewery: Tasmania's most northerly brewery, with a taproom on a rise above the pastures; a venue, not a sight.

name: Festival of King Island
note: Festival: two-day summer music and food festival, early February each year; an annual event, not a permanent spot.

name: Penny Royal Adventures
note: Operator: adventure tours on King Island, listed under While You Are In The Area; an operator, not a place.

name: Reid Rocks
note: Wildlife: reef 12 km offshore with a major Australian fur seal colony, seen on boat trips; named in a search summary, not in the fetched visitor pages.

name: Flinders Island
note: Island destination: largest island of the Furneaux Group, reached by Sharp Airlines from Launceston and Melbourne or a freight ferry from Bridport; the base for everything on Flinders Island.

name: Whitemark
note: Town: the island's largest town and administrative centre, with the Flinders Wharf, the bakery and most services.

name: Lady Barron
note: Town: the southern settlement and ferry port at Lady Barron, with the island's general store.

name: Killiecrankie
note: Town: northern settlement on the island's north-east coast, the start of the coastal walk to The Dock and the topaz beaches.

name: Killiecrankie Bay
note: Beach: bay where visitors search the sand at low tide for semi-precious topaz, known as Killiecrankie diamonds; near-duplicate of Killiecrankie possible.

name: Killiecrankie to The Dock Coast Walk
note: Walk: rocky coastal walk from Killiecrankie to The Dock, past a sea arch at Stackys Bight and Old Man's Head; a route, not a single place.

name: The Dock
note: Coastal spot: rocky shore at the end of the Killiecrankie walk, with swimming and snorkelling.

name: Old Man's Head
note: Rock: towering boulder on the Killiecrankie to The Dock coastal walk.

name: Stackys Bight
note: Coastal feature: sea arch on the Killiecrankie to The Dock walk; part of that walk.

name: Strzelecki National Park
note: National park: Tasmania's Strzelecki National Park on Flinders Island's south-west, with the Strzelecki Peaks, Trousers Point and Castle Rock; entry charged per vehicle.

name: Strzelecki Peaks
note: Mountain walk: 4-5 hour return Great Short Walk to the 756 m summit of Mount Strzelecki, the island's highest point; steep, and the summit can be cold and windy.

name: Trousers Point
note: Beach and walk: turquoise beach with a Great Short Walk loop, snorkelling and a walk-in campground at its southern end, in Strzelecki National Park.

name: Castle Rock
note: Walk: beach-hop to towering Castle Rock, one of Tasmania's 60 Great Short Walks.

name: Mount Killiecrankie
note: Mountain: climb in the island's north, named alongside Mount Boyes as a hike option.

name: Mount Boyes
note: Mountain: climb in the island's north, named alongside Mount Killiecrankie as a hike option.

name: Mount Tanner
note: Lookout: drive to the top for views over the island; Walkers Lookout is named nearby as a sunrise stop.

name: Long Point
note: Coastal wetland: tidal salt marsh on the self-guided north Flinders drive; named in a search summary, not in the fetched visitor pages.

name: Wybalenna Chapel
note: Historic site: chapel and cemetery of Wybalenna, the 1830s-40s settlement where Aboriginal Tasmanians were exiled; the island's most sombre site.

name: Furneaux Museum
note: Museum: island history at Emita, with a muttonbirding shed replica, the Whitemark police cells and an anchor from the Sydney Cove.

name: Palana Beach
note: Beach: white beach at the far north of the island, one of the island's main swimming beaches.

name: Yellow Beach
note: Beach: white beach at the south of the island, named as the southern end of the island's beach run.

name: Unavale Vineyard
note: Winery: cellar door at one of the island's three small vineyards; a cellar door, not a sight.

name: Furneaux Distillery
note: Distillery: gin and peated whisky made from island peat, tours by appointment; a distillery, not a sight.

name: The Flinders Wharf
note: Restaurant: larder-restaurant and distillery in Whitemark on the site of the old wharf storage shed; a restaurant, not a sight.

name: Flinders Island Adventures
note: Operator: tours to the offshore islands and fishing trips from Flinders Island; an operator, not a place.

name: Roaring 40s Kayaking
note: Operator: week-long sea-kayaking trips around the island's shores and offshore islands; an operator, not a place.

name: Cape Barren Island
note: Island: second-largest of the Furneaux Group, Aboriginal community island with restricted visitor access; no visitor source names it as a stop.

name: Kent Group National Park
note: National park: marine and island national park in Bass Strait, a haven for sea lions, reached by boat only; Wikivoyage calls it adventurous.
